You are ML Intern, an ML engineering assistant with 18 tools for training, fine-tuning, data processing, inference, and evaluation on the Hugging Face (HF) ecosystem. Your goal is to complete what the user requested with zero errors. You are fully autonomous — research, validate, implement, and deliver results without asking for unnecessary confirmation. # Your knowledge of HF libraries is outdated You do not know current APIs for TRL, Transformers, PEFT, Trackio, or other HF libraries. Your internal knowledge WILL produce wrong imports, wrong argument names, and wrong trainer configurations. Before writing any ML implementation code, start from the literature. The parallel research sub-agents can crawl papers, read their methodology sections, trace citation graphs, and extract the exact datasets and training recipes that produced published results. This is your primary advantage — use it. Your default workflow for any ML task: 1. Find the landmark paper(s) for the task or domain 2. Crawl their citation graphs to find recent downstream work 3. Read methodology sections (not abstracts) of the most promising papers — especially recent ones with strong results, lot of citations, and publications in high-impact conferences 4. Extract the recipe: what dataset, what training method, what hyperparameters produced those results 5. Validate and use those datasets for training ``` research({"task": "Literature crawl for [task]. Start from [paper/topic]. Crawl citation graph for recent downstream papers. Read their methodology sections (3, 4, 5) — extract the exact datasets, training methods, and hyperparameters that produced their best results. Attribute every finding to a specific result (e.g. 'Dataset X + method Y → 85.3% on benchmark Z'). Also find working code examples using current TRL/Transformers APIs.", "context": "User wants to [goal]. We need the best training recipe backed by published results."}) ``` The sub-agent knows how to use github_find_examples, github_read_file, explore_hf_docs, fetch_hf_docs, hf_inspect_dataset, and hf_papers (with citation_graph, read_paper, snippet_search, find_datasets). Be specific in your task description — name anchor papers or arxiv IDs when you have them. You can also call research tools directly (explore_hf_docs, github_read_file, etc.) for quick lookups. Skip research only for trivial non-code operations. # Mistakes you WILL make without research HALLUCINATED IMPORTS: You will import from modules that were renamed or removed. Example: old TRL trainer class names, deprecated Transformers APIs, wrong trackio config field names. Fix: read a current example script first. WRONG TRAINER ARGUMENTS: You will pass configuration arguments that don't exist in current trainer versions. Fix: fetch the actual trainer/config docs via explore_hf_docs + fetch_hf_docs. WRONG DATASET FORMAT: You will assume column names without checking. Training fails with KeyError. Fix: call hf_inspect_dataset or hub_repo_details and verify columns match the training method. DEFAULT TIMEOUT KILLS JOBS: You will leave timeout at the default 30m for training jobs. Training takes hours. The job gets killed and all progress is lost. Fix: set timeout based on model size (minimum 2h for any training). LOST MODELS: You will forget push_to_hub=True and hub_model_id in training config. Job storage is ephemeral — the filesystem is deleted when the job ends. Without push_to_hub, the trained model is permanently lost. BATCH FAILURES: You will submit all ablation/batch jobs at once without testing that one works first. All will fail for the same bug. Fix: submit ONE job first, verify it completes successfully, then submit the rest. SILENT DATASET SUBSTITUTION: When a requested dataset fails to load, you will silently switch to a different one without telling the user. Fix: if the requested dataset isn't available, tell the user and ask what to do. PREFER HUB KERNELS OVER COMPILING ATTENTION: Do NOT pip install 'flash-attn' to enable flash_attention_2 building from source can take many minutes to hours and often fails on the job's CUDA/PyTorch combo. Instead, use the HF `kernels` library (`pip install kernels`, already pulled in by recent TRL) and load a prebuilt attention kernel from the Hub via `attn_implementation`. Examples: `AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(..., attn_implementation="kernels-community/flash-attn2")`, or `kernels-community/vllm-flash-attn3`, or `kernels-community/paged-attention`. With TRL/SFT scripts you can pass `--attn_implementation kernels-community/flash-attn2` on the CLI. Search additional kernels at https://huggingface.co/models?other=kernel. Only `pip install` extra packages (and document why) when no Hub kernel covers the need. SCOPE-CHANGING FIXES: Avoid at all costs! When you hit an error (especially OOM), you will try "creative" workarounds that change what the user asked for and/or change the training task itself — switching full SFT to LoRA on OOM, reducing max_length (silently truncates training data and changes what the model learns), disabling monitoring instead of fixing it. Do not do this. Fix errors with the minimal change that preserves the user's original request and are grounded in research and examples. If the original approach genuinely cannot work, explain why and ask the user for input before changing methods, sequence length, training approach or any other part of the task. # When writing ML code Required sequence before any training/fine-tuning/inference script: 1. Use `research` tool to find working examples, read docs, and get current API patterns 2. Validate dataset: hf_inspect_dataset or hub_repo_details to confirm column names and format 3. Validate model: hub_repo_details to confirm model exists, correct architecture/size/tokenizer Training logging: always set disable_tqdm=True, logging_strategy="steps", and logging_first_step=True in your TrainingArguments/SFTConfig so loss values are printed as plain text lines you can grep, not hidden inside tqdm progress bars. Dataset format requirements by training method: SFT: "messages", "text", or "prompt"/"completion" DPO: "prompt", "chosen", "rejected" GRPO: "prompt" # Trackio Trackio is natively integrated with Transformers Trainer and all TRL trainers — the built-in TrackioCallback handles init/log/finish. In TrainingArguments/SFTConfig/DPOConfig/GRPOConfig set: report_to="trackio" run_name="" # e.g. "sft_qwen3-4b_lr2e-5_bs128" project="" # keeps related runs grouped so you can compare them trackio_space_id="/ml-intern-<8-char-id>" # creates a public dashboard Space `project` and `trackio_space_id` can also be set via TRACKIO_PROJECT / TRACKIO_SPACE_ID env vars. Alerts are how iterations decide what to change. Use trackio.alert(title, text, level) at every decision point in training. Levels: ERROR — stop and change approach (divergence, NaN, OOM) WARN — tweak hyperparameters (overfitting, early stopping, KL spike, reward collapse, slow convergence) INFO — milestones (training complete, target reached, checkpoint saved) Always include numeric values and an actionable suggestion in `text`, e.g. "loss=12.4 at step 200 — lr likely too high, try ×0.1". A future call must be able to parse it and act on it. To add alerts under Trainer/SFTTrainer/GRPOTrainer, pass a custom TrainerCallback via `callbacks=[...]` that calls trackio.alert() inside `on_log` (training metrics like loss, reward, kl) and `on_evaluate` (eval metrics — only available here, not in `on_log`). Keep each `if` simple: one metric, one threshold. Conditions stay easy to adjust between runs. Read alerts back between runs instead of parsing thousands of metric values. CLI — always use --json: trackio get alerts --project

--run --json trackio get alerts --project

--since --json # incremental polling trackio get run --project

--run --json trackio get metric --project

--run --metric --json trackio list runs --project

--json Python: api = trackio.Api(); api.alerts(

, run=, since=); api.runs(

) (each run has .name, .config, .alerts()). Drive the next config from prior alerts: diverged → lr × 0.1 overfitting → weight_decay × 10 or reduce capacity early stopping → lr × 0.5 or adjust schedule high accuracy → refine around current config Read prior config via api.runs(...).config and only mutate keys the alerts justify changing. # Data audit Before working with any dataset, audit it first. Do not assume you know what the data looks like — inspect it. Use hf_inspect_dataset to check: schema/columns, number of rows per split, value distributions for key columns, sample rows. Surface anything notable: class imbalance, missing values, unexpected formats, outliers, duplicate rows, etc. Looking at data is the best way to boost performance of any ML model plus it reduces the likelihood of failed jobs later. # When submitting a training job Before calling hf_jobs, output a pre-flight check: - Reference implementation: [which example you based this on] - Dataset format verified: [columns confirmed via hf_inspect_dataset/hub_repo_details] - push_to_hub=True and hub_model_id set - timeout: [value] (based on: [model size] on [hardware]) - Trackio monitoring included and deploying metrics to a public Space If you cannot fill in all items, stop and complete the missing steps first. For batch/ablation jobs: submit ONE job first. Check logs to confirm it starts training successfully. Only then submit the remaining jobs. Never submit all at once. Hardware sizing: 1-3B params: a10g-largex2 7-13B params: a100-large 30B+ params: l40sx4 or a100x4 70B+ params: a100x8 Note: a10g-small and a10g-large have the SAME 24GB GPU memory. The difference is CPU/RAM only. # Sandbox-first development A private cpu-basic sandbox is already available for normal code execution in each session. For non-trivial scripts, develop and test there before launching via hf_jobs: write script → pip install → test with small run using bash/read/write/edit → fix errors → launch via hf_jobs at scale Do NOT call sandbox_create before normal CPU work. Call sandbox_create only when you need GPU hardware or another non-default sandbox tier. Use GPU sandbox (t4-small minimum) when testing code that uses CUDA, bf16, or model loading. CPU sandboxes cannot test GPU code paths. # When a task has 3+ steps Use plan_tool to track progress. One task in_progress at a time. Mark completed immediately after finishing. Update frequently to show the user what you're doing. # Error recovery When something fails: - Diagnose the actual error. Read the full error message and logs. - Do not retry the exact same thing. Identify what needs to change. - If an API/import error: check documentation for the correct API. - If an OOM error: (1) reduce per_device_train_batch_size and increase gradient_accumulation_steps proportionally to keep effective batch size identical, (2) enable gradient_checkpointing=True, (3) upgrade to larger GPU (a10gx4→a100→a100x4→a100x8). Do NOT switch training methods (e.g. SFT→LoRA) or reduce max_length — those change what the user gets. If OOM happens in sandbox, create a new sandbox with larger GPU hardware. - Never change the user's requested approach (training method, dataset, model, sequence length) without explicit approval. - If a tool call fails repeatedly for the same reason: stop and try a different approach. - Never silently substitute resources (datasets, models) — tell the user if something isn't available. # Task completion Before ending your turn, verify: - Did you actually DO what the user asked, not just explain what you would do? - If something failed: did you diagnose and fix it, or at minimum explain what went wrong and ask for user input? - For training jobs: did you include a working Trackio dashboard URL? Do not stop after describing what you plan to do. Continue calling tools until the task is verifiably done. Do not mark plan tasks as completed if they failed or are only partially done. # Autonomous / headless mode When running autonomously (no human in the loop), you MUST follow these rules: NEVER respond with only text. Every response MUST include at least one tool call. If you have nothing to do, check the plan, verify outputs or plan ahead. A text-only response ends the agent loop permanently — there is no human to re-prompt you. NEVER STOP WORKING. Do NOT decide you are "done" while time remains. The human is not watching — they expect you to use the ENTIRE time budget productively. Do NOT ask "should I continue?" or "is this a good stopping point?" — there is nobody to answer. You run until the timer expires or you are manually killed. Your workflow is a loop, not a checklist. Once you have a working result, KEEP ITERATING: LOOP UNTIL TIME RUNS OUT: 1. Research the approach (read docs, find examples, check current APIs) 2. Implement the solution (write code, set up training) 3. Train and evaluate 4. Save the model to the required output location / push it to Hugging Face Hub 5. Improve: tune hyperparameters, try different data, adjust the training recipe, try a different approach entirely 6. Go to step 1 HYPERPARAMETER TUNING: Do not tune hyperparameters by hand one-at-a-time. Write a script that launches a sweep over a grid of values (learning rate, epochs, batch size, etc.) and evaluates each run automatically. One well-designed sweep script beats ten manual experiments. If you run out of ideas: go back to the literature. Crawl citation graphs deeper — find papers you haven't read yet, read their methodology sections, extract new datasets or training tricks. Look for papers that cite your current approach and improved on it. Try combining recipes from different papers. Re-read the task prompt for angles you missed. Re-read the training logs for clues. There is always a paper you haven't read yet, and it probably has a better dataset. Check the remaining time periodically with the timer command specified in the task prompt. Budget your time: reserve at least 10 minutes at the end for final evaluation and model saving. The task is NOT done until: - The required output exists (e.g. final model, metrics reached, dataset updated etc) - You have evaluated the model and confirmed it works # Communication - Be concise and direct. No filler, no restating what the user said. - One-word answers when appropriate for simple questions. - Always include direct Hub URLs when referencing models, datasets, Spaces, or jobs. - For errors: state what went wrong, why, and what you're doing to fix it. - Do not over-explain or present elaborate option menus for simple tasks. When the user's intent is clear, act on it. Present options only when there's genuine ambiguity. - Use the `notify` tool only when the user explicitly asked for out-of-band notifications or when the task clearly requires reporting to a configured messaging destination. Do not use it for routine chat updates. # Tool usage - Execute multiple independent tool calls in parallel when possible. - HF_TOKEN is automatically available in job secrets — no need to include it extra. - For training monitoring: include Trackio in the script and provide the dashboard URL. - For private/gated datasets: HF_TOKEN is needed — it's auto-loaded into job secrets. # CLI / Local mode You are running as a local CLI tool on the user's machine. There is NO sandbox — bash, read, write, and edit operate directly on the local filesystem. Working directory: /root/v2rmp Use absolute paths or paths relative to the working directory. Do NOT use /app/ paths — that is a sandbox convention that does not apply here. The sandbox_create tool is NOT available. Run code directly with bash. 1	# /// script
     2	# requires-python = ">=3.11"
     3	# dependencies = [
     4	#     "safetensors>=0.4",
     5	#     "numpy>=1.24",
     6	# ]
     7	# ///
     8	
     9	"""
    10	Offline training pipeline for v2rmp Neural Models — TRAINED ON REAL SOLVER DATA.
    11	
    12	Consumes data/training_data.jsonl generated by `cargo run --bin generate-training-data`.
    13	Each line is a JSON object with:
    14	  - features: 28-dim Vec<float>
    15	  - best_solver: string
    16	  - best_distance_km: float
    17	  - solver_dists: [{solver: str, distance: float}, ...]
    18	  - n_stops, n_vehicles, objective
    19	
    20	Trains:
    21	  1. Solver Selector: COST-SENSITIVE regression (predicts regret per solver)
    22	     Inference: argmin regret → best solver. This directly minimizes distance.
    23	  2. Quality Predictor: regression on best_distance_km + gap vs default solver
    24	  3. AutoML Predictor: regression on heuristic-informed hyperparams
    25	  4. Move Scorer: regression on synthetic move data
    26	  5. GraphSAGE: placeholder identity weights
    27	
    28	Exports Candle-compatible safetensors.
    29	"""
    30	
    31	import os
    32	import json
    33	import numpy as np
    34	from safetensors.numpy import save_file
    35	
    36	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    37	# 0. Load real training data
    38	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    39	
    40	def load_training_data(path="data/training_data.jsonl"):
    41	    """Load JSON-lines training data produced by Rust generator."""
    42	    entries = []
    43	    with open(path, "r") as f:
    44	        for line in f:
    45	            line = line.strip()
    46	            if not line:
    47	                continue
    48	            entries.append(json.loads(line))
    49	    return entries
    50	
    51	SOLVER_IDS = ["default", "clarke_wright", "sweep", "or_opt", "two_opt", "neural_guided"]
    52	
    53	def prepare_real_labels(entries):
    54	    """Convert raw entries into numpy matrices for training.
    55	    
    56	    COST-SENSITIVE formulation: the selector predicts REGRET per solver
    57	    (distance above the best). At inference we pick argmin regret.
    58	    """
    59	    n = len(entries)
    60	    X = np.zeros((n, 28), dtype=np.float32)
    61	    Y_cost      = np.zeros((n, 6), dtype=np.float32)   # regret per solver
    62	    Y_quality   = np.zeros((n, 2), dtype=np.float32)
    63	    Y_automl    = np.zeros((n, 5), dtype=np.float32)
    64	
    65	    move_instances = []
    66	
    67	    for i, e in enumerate(entries):
    68	        X[i] = np.array(e["features"], dtype=np.float32)
    69	
    70	        # Build solver-distance map
    71	        dists = {sd["solver"]: float(sd["distance"]) for sd in e["solver_dists"]}
    72	        best_dist = min(dists.values())
    73	
    74	        # Cost-sensitive target: regret = (dist_j - best_dist) / best_dist
    75	        for j, sid in enumerate(SOLVER_IDS):
    76	            d = dists.get(sid, best_dist * 2.0)
    77	            regret = (d - best_dist) / (best_dist + 1e-6)
    78	            Y_cost[i, j] = regret
    79	
    80	        # Quality predictor labels
    81	        worst_dist = max(dists.values())
    82	        if worst_dist > best_dist:
    83	            normalized_gap = (worst_dist - best_dist) / (worst_dist - best_dist + 1e-6)
    84	            gap_pct = normalized_gap * 50.0
    85	        else:
    86	            gap_pct = 0.0
    87	
    88	        tour_norm = min(best_dist / 5000.0, 1.0)
    89	        Y_quality[i, 0] = gap_pct / 50.0
    90	        Y_quality[i, 1] = tour_norm
    91	
    92	        # AutoML labels
    93	        n_stops_norm = X[i, 0]
    94	        density_norm = X[i, 5]
    95	        capacity_ratio = X[i, 19]
    96	        Y_automl[i, 0] = n_stops_norm
    97	        Y_automl[i, 1] = 0.3 + density_norm * 0.4
    98	        Y_automl[i, 2] = 0.1 + capacity_ratio * 0.3
    99	        Y_automl[i, 3] = 0.9
   100	        Y_automl[i, 4] = 0.15
   101	
   102	        moves = generate_synthetic_moves_from_features(X[i], n_stops_norm)
   103	        move_instances.extend(moves)
   104	
   105	    return X, Y_cost, Y_quality, Y_automl, move_instances
   106	
   107	def generate_synthetic_moves_from_features(features, n_stops_norm):
   108	    """Generate synthetic 2-opt move features heuristically from instance stats."""
   109	    moves = []
   110	    n = max(int(n_stops_norm * 500), 10)
   111	    for _ in range(min(n, 50)):
   112	        d_ab = np.random.rand() * 10.0
   113	        d_cd = np.random.rand() * 10.0
   114	        d_ac = np.random.rand() * 10.0
   115	        d_bd = np.random.rand() * 10.0
   116	        delta = (d_ac + d_bd) - (d_ab + d_cd)
   117	        avg_edge = max((d_ab + d_cd + d_ac + d_bd) / 4.0, 1e-6)
   118	
   119	        feat = np.zeros(16, dtype=np.float32)
   120	        feat[0] = d_ab
   121	        feat[1] = d_cd
   122	        feat[2] = d_ac
   123	        feat[3] = d_bd
   124	        feat[4] = delta
   125	        feat[5] = d_ab / avg_edge
   126	        feat[6] = d_cd / avg_edge
   127	        feat[7] = d_ac / avg_edge
   128	        feat[8] = d_bd / avg_edge
   129	        feat[9] = np.random.rand() * 20.0
   130	        feat[10] = np.random.rand()
   131	        feat[11] = np.random.rand() * n_stops_norm * 10
   132	        feat[12] = feat[11] / max(n_stops_norm * 10, 1.0)
   133	        feat[13] = np.random.rand()
   134	        feat[14] = np.random.rand()
   135	        feat[15] = 1.0 if delta < -1e-6 else 0.0
   136	
   137	        score = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(delta))
   138	        moves.append((feat, score))
   139	    return moves
   140	
   141	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   142	# 1. Core Neural Components
   143	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   144	
   145	def relu(x):
   146	    return np.maximum(0, x)
   147	
   148	def relu_deriv(x):
   149	    return (x > 0).astype(np.float32)
   150	
   151	def softmax(x):
   152	    x_max = np.max(x, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
   153	    exps = np.exp(x - x_max)
   154	    return exps / np.sum(exps, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
   155	
   156	class AdamOptimizer:
   157	    def __init__(self, params, lr=0.001, beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999, eps=1e-8):
   158	        self.lr = lr
   159	        self.beta1 = beta1
   160	        self.beta2 = beta2
   161	        self.eps = eps
   162	        self.m = {k: np.zeros_like(v) for k, v in params.items()}
   163	        self.v = {k: np.zeros_like(v) for k, v in params.items()}
   164	        self.t = 0
   165	
   166	    def step(self, params, grads):
   167	        self.t += 1
   168	        for k in params.keys():
   169	            self.m[k] = self.beta1 * self.m[k] + (1 - self.beta1) * grads[k]
   170	            self.v[k] = self.beta2 * self.v[k] + (1 - self.beta2) * (grads[k] ** 2)
   171	            m_hat = self.m[k] / (1 - self.beta1 ** self.t)
   172	            v_hat = self.v[k] / (1 - self.beta2 ** self.t)
   173	            params[k] -= self.lr * m_hat / (np.sqrt(v_hat) + self.eps)
   174	
   175	class NumpyMLP:
   176	    def __init__(self, layer_sizes, prefix="lin"):
   177	        self.layer_sizes = layer_sizes
   178	        self.weights = {}
   179	        self.prefix = prefix
   180	        for i in range(len(layer_sizes) - 1):
   181	            n_in = layer_sizes[i]
   182	            n_out = layer_sizes[i + 1]
   183	            std = np.sqrt(2.0 / n_in)
   184	            self.weights[f'{prefix}{i+1}.weight'] = np.random.normal(0, std, (n_out, n_in)).astype(np.float32)
   185	            self.weights[f'{prefix}{i+1}.bias'] = np.zeros(n_out, dtype=np.float32)
   186	
   187	    def forward(self, x):
   188	        activations = [x]
   189	        zs = []
   190	        for i in range(len(self.layer_sizes) - 1):
   191	            w = self.weights[f'{self.prefix}{i+1}.weight']
   192	            b = self.weights[f'{self.prefix}{i+1}.bias']
   193	            z = np.dot(activations[-1], w.T) + b
   194	            zs.append(z)
   195	            if i < len(self.layer_sizes) - 2:
   196	                activations.append(relu(z))
   197	            else:
   198	                activations.append(z)
   199	        return activations, zs
   200	
   201	    def backward(self, activations, zs, y_grad):
   202	        grads = {}
   203	        delta = y_grad
   204	        for i in reversed(range(len(self.layer_sizes) - 1)):
   205	            w = self.weights[f'{self.prefix}{i+1}.weight']
   206	            grads[f'{self.prefix}{i+1}.weight'] = np.dot(delta.T, activations[i])
   207	            grads[f'{self.prefix}{i+1}.bias'] = np.sum(delta, axis=0)
   208	            if i > 0:
   209	                delta = np.dot(delta, w) * relu_deriv(zs[i - 1])
   210	        return grads
   211	
   212	def train_mlp_model(name, input_dim, hidden_dims, output_dim, X, Y, task='regression',
   213	                    epochs=300, lr=0.001, batch_size=16):
   214	    print(f"Training {name}...")
   215	    layer_sizes = [input_dim] + hidden_dims + [output_dim]
   216	    model = NumpyMLP(layer_sizes)
   217	    optimizer = AdamOptimizer(model.weights, lr=lr)
   218	
   219	    n = X.shape[0]
   220	    n_batches = max(n // batch_size, 1)
   221	
   222	    best_val_loss = float('inf')
   223	    patience = 30
   224	    no_improve = 0
   225	
   226	    split = int(0.8 * n)
   227	    idx = np.random.permutation(n)
   228	    train_idx, val_idx = idx[:split], idx[split:]
   229	    X_train, Y_train = X[train_idx], Y[train_idx]
   230	    X_val, Y_val = X[val_idx], Y[val_idx]
   231	
   232	    for epoch in range(epochs):
   233	        epoch_loss = 0.0
   234	        idx_s = np.random.permutation(X_train.shape[0])
   235	        for b in range(n_batches):
   236	            sl = slice(b * batch_size, (b + 1) * batch_size)
   237	            x_b, y_b = X_train[idx_s][sl], Y_train[idx_s][sl]
   238	            if x_b.shape[0] == 0:
   239	                continue
   240	            activations, zs = model.forward(x_b)
   241	            pred = activations[-1]
   242	
   243	            if task == 'classification':
   244	                probs = softmax(pred)
   245	                loss = -np.mean(np.sum(y_b * np.log(probs + 1e-10), axis=1))
   246	                y_grad = (probs - y_b) / x_b.shape[0]
   247	            else:
   248	                loss = np.mean((pred - y_b) ** 2)
   249	                y_grad = 2 * (pred - y_b) / x_b.shape[0]
   250	
   251	            grads = model.backward(activations, zs, y_grad)
   252	            optimizer.step(model.weights, grads)
   253	            epoch_loss += loss
   254	
   255	        if X_val.shape[0] > 0:
   256	            activations, _ = model.forward(X_val)
   257	            pred = activations[-1]
   258	            if task == 'classification':
   259	                probs = softmax(pred)
   260	                val_loss = -np.mean(np.sum(Y_val * np.log(probs + 1e-10), axis=1))
   261	                acc = np.mean(np.argmax(probs, axis=1) == np.argmax(Y_val, axis=1))
   262	            else:
   263	                val_loss = np.mean((pred - Y_val) ** 2)
   264	                acc = None
   265	
   266	            if val_loss < best_val_loss:
   267	                best_val_loss = val_loss
   268	                no_improve = 0
   269	            else:
   270	                no_improve += 1
   271	
   272	            if epoch % 30 == 0:
   273	                if task == 'classification':
   274	                    print(f"  Epoch {epoch:3d} — loss={epoch_loss / n_batches:.6f} val={val_loss:.6f} acc={acc:.3f}")
   275	                else:
   276	                    print(f"  Epoch {epoch:3d} — loss={epoch_loss / n_batches:.6f} val={val_loss:.6f}")
   277	
   278	            if no_improve > patience:
   279	                print(f"  Early stopping at epoch {epoch}")
   280	                break
   281	
   282	    if task == 'classification':
   283	        activations, _ = model.forward(X)
   284	        pred = np.argmax(softmax(activations[-1]), axis=1)
   285	        true_lbl = np.argmax(Y, axis=1)
   286	        print(f"  Final accuracy: {np.mean(pred == true_lbl):.4f}")
   287	    else:
   288	        activations, _ = model.forward(X)
   289	        pred = activations[-1]
   290	        mse = np.mean((pred - Y) ** 2)
   291	        print(f"  Final MSE: {mse:.6f}")
   292	
   293	    return model.weights
   294	
   295	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   296	# 2. Main
   297	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   298	
   299	if __name__ == "__main__":
   300	    os.makedirs("models", exist_ok=True)
   301	    np.random.seed(42)
   302	
   303	    print("Loading real solver training data...")
   304	    entries = load_training_data("data/training_data.jsonl")
   305	    print(f"  Loaded {len(entries)} instances")
   306	
   307	    X, Y_cost, Y_qual, Y_auto, move_instances = prepare_real_labels(entries)
   308	    print(f"  Feature matrix: {X.shape}")
   309	
   310	    # --- 1. Solver Selector (cost-sensitive regret regression) ---
   311	    selector_weights = train_mlp_model(
   312	        "Solver Selector (cost-sensitive)", 28, [128, 64], 6, X, Y_cost,
   313	        task='regression', epochs=500, lr=0.001
   314	    )
   315	    save_file(selector_weights, "models/solver_selector.safetensors")
   316	
   317	    # Sanity-check argmin-regret accuracy
   318	    test_model = NumpyMLP([28, 128, 64, 6])
   319	    test_model.weights = selector_weights
   320	    activations, _ = test_model.forward(X)
   321	    pred_idx = np.argmin(activations[-1], axis=1)
   322	    true_idx = np.argmin(Y_cost, axis=1)
   323	    print(f"  Argmin-regret accuracy: {np.mean(pred_idx == true_idx):.4f}")
   324	    for j, sid in enumerate(SOLVER_IDS):
   325	        n_pred = int(np.sum(pred_idx == j))
   326	        n_true = int(np.sum(true_idx == j))
   327	        print(f"    {sid:15s} pred={n_pred:4d} true={n_true:4d}")
   328	
   329	    # --- 2. Quality Predictor ---
   330	    quality_weights = train_mlp_model(
   331	        "Quality Predictor", 28, [64, 32], 2, X, Y_qual, task='regression', epochs=400, lr=0.001
   332	    )
   333	    save_file(quality_weights, "models/quality_predictor.safetensors")
   334	
   335	    # --- 3. AutoML Predictor ---
   336	    automl_weights = train_mlp_model(
   337	        "AutoML Predictor", 28, [64], 5, X, Y_auto, task='regression', epochs=300, lr=0.001
   338	    )
   339	    save_file(automl_weights, "models/automl.safetensors")
   340	
   341	    # --- 4. Move Scorer ---
   342	    move_X = np.array([m[0] for m in move_instances], dtype=np.float32)
   343	    move_Y = np.array([[m[1]] for m in move_instances], dtype=np.float32)
   344	    move_weights = train_mlp_model(
   345	        "Move Scorer", 16, [32, 16], 1, move_X, move_Y, task='regression', epochs=500, lr=0.001
   346	    )
   347	    save_file(move_weights, "models/move_scorer.safetensors")
   348	
   349	    # --- 5. GraphSAGE Placeholder ---
   350	    sage_weights = {
   351	        'conv1.lin_l.weight': np.eye(64, 10).astype(np.float32) * 0.1,
   352	        'conv1.lin_l.bias': np.zeros(64, dtype=np.float32),
   353	        'conv1.lin_r.weight': np.eye(64, 10).astype(np.float32) * 0.1,
   354	        'conv2.lin_l.weight': np.eye(64, 64).astype(np.float32) * 0.1,
   355	        'conv2.lin_l.bias': np.zeros(64, dtype=np.float32),
   356	        'conv2.lin_r.weight': np.eye(64, 64).astype(np.float32) * 0.1,
   357	    }
   358	    save_file(sage_weights, "models/graph_embed.safetensors")
   359	
   360	    print("\nTraining complete on REAL SOLVER DATA. Models exported to models/")
   361	    print(f"  Selector: cost-sensitive regret regression on {len(entries)} instances")

1	# v2rmp ML/AI Integration Architecture
     2	
     3	## Executive Summary
     4	
     5	This document describes the heavy ML/AI integration into v2rmp (rmpca), a Rust CLI/TUI/GUI tool for route optimization. The integration upgrades the existing rule-based ML modules to learned models, adds graph embeddings, route quality prediction, NLP query parsing, and AutoML hyperparameter tuning — all backed by published research.
     6	
     7	## Current State (Audit)
     8	
     9	### Existing ML/AI Touchpoints
    10	
    11	| Module | File | Current Capabilities | Status |
    12	|--------|------|---------------------|-----|
    13	| `ml` | `src/core/ml/` | Neural solver selection, quality prediction, AutoML, GraphSAGE | Implemented (v0.5.0) |
    14	| `training` | `train_models.py` | NumPy-based offline training pipeline for all models | Implemented (v0.5.0) |
    15	| `embed` | `src/core/embed.rs` | BERT text embeddings via Candle (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5) | Existing |
    16	| MCP Server | `src/bin/rmpca-mcp-server.rs` | 15+ tools incl. `predict_solver`, `score_route`, `route_embedding` | Upgraded to learned models |
    17	| VRP Solvers | `src/core/vrp/solvers/*.rs` | 5 classical heuristics (Clarke-Wright, Sweep, 2-Opt, Or-Opt, Default) | No neural solver, no learned local search guidance. |
    18	| Elevation | `src/core/elevation/` | DEM GeoTIFF queries, fuel estimation | No ML-based terrain-aware weighting. |
    19	
    20	### Architecture Gaps
    21	
    22	1. **No learned solver selector** — `predict_solver` uses hand-tuned weights (density > 5.0 → +0.15, etc.). No data-driven training.
    23	2. **No instance-aware AutoML** — solver hyperparameters are hard-coded. No per-instance tuning.
    24	3. **No graph embeddings for road networks** — road segments are treated as raw edges. No learned representations.
    25	4. **No route quality prediction** — quality is only scored *after* solving. No early-stopping or solver-spawning guidance.
    26	5. **No NLP query parser** — the `agent` command takes JSON only. No natural-language routing requests.
    27	6. **No learned local search guidance** — 2-Opt/Or-Opt use random/exhaustive moves. No neural move selector.
    28	
    29	---
    30	
    31	## Proposed Architecture
    32	
    33	### Module Map
    34	
    35	```
    36	src/core/
    37	├── ml/                          # NEW: ML module directory
    38	│   ├── mod.rs                   # Re-exports, shared types
    39	│   ├── selector.rs              # Neural/ensemble solver selector
    40	│   ├── features.rs              # Instance feature extraction (research-backed)
    41	│   ├── quality_predictor.rs     # Route quality prediction before solve
    42	│   ├── automl.rs                # Instance-aware hyperparameter regression
    43	│   └── graph_embed.rs           # Road network graph embeddings
    44	├── embed.rs                     # EXISTING: text embeddings (BERT)
    45	├── nlp.rs                       # NEW: NL query → VRP config parser
    46	├── vrp/                         # EXISTING
    47	│   ├── solvers/
    48	│   │   ├── neural_guided.rs     # NEW: neural-guided local search wrapper
    49	│   │   └── ...
    50	│   └── ...
    51	└── ...
    52	```
    53	
    54	### 1. Neural Solver Selector (`ml::selector`)
    55	
    56	**Replaces**: `src/core/ml.rs::predict_solver()`  
    57	**Research basis**: Instance-Aware Parameter Configuration (2605.00572, 2026) + RouteFinder (2406.15007, 2024)
    58	
    59	**Design**:
    60	- **Feature extraction**: 28-dim instance feature vector (see `ml::features`).
    61	- **Model**: Small MLP (2 hidden layers, 128→64→5) implemented in Candle.
    62	- **Output**: Softmax over 5 solver IDs + confidence.
    63	- **Training**: Offline on CVRPLIB + synthetic instances. Labels = best solver in fixed time budget.
    64	- **Inference**: ~0.1ms per instance (pure Rust/Candle).
    65	
    66	**Feature vector (28-dim)**:
    67	```
    68	# Geometric (8)
    69	n_stops_norm, n_vehicles_norm, avg_pairwise_km_norm, lat_spread_norm,
    70	lon_spread_norm, density_norm, area_km2_norm, depot_centroid_dist_norm
    71	
    72	# Graph (8) — from kNN(k=10) graph of stops
    73	knn_avg_degree, knn_max_degree, knn_clustering, knn_diameter_norm,
    74	knn_mst_weight_norm, knn_avg_shortest_path, knn_spectral_gap, knn_assortativity
    75	
    76	# Demand (4)
    77	total_demand_norm, demand_std_norm, tight_capacity_flag, capacity_ratio
    78	
    79	# Distance matrix stats (4)
    80	dist_mean_norm, dist_std_norm, dist_skewness, depot_dist_mean_norm
    81	
    82	# Objective & interaction (4)
    83	objective_onehot[4], stops_per_vehicle_norm, spread_x_demand_interaction
    84	```
    85	
    86	### 2. Instance-Aware AutoML (`ml::automl`)
    87	
    88	**Replaces**: hard-coded solver hyperparameters  
    89	**Research basis**: Instance-Aware Parameter Configuration (2605.00572)
    90	
    91	**Design**:
    92	- **Problem**: Predict best hyperparameters (e.g., `max_iterations`, `temperature` for SA, `tabu_tenure`) given instance features.
    93	- **Model**: Separate Ridge regression per hyperparameter, or a single multi-output MLP.
    94	- **Training**: Run `irace`-style offline tuning on a diverse instance set, record best configs, train regressor.
    95	- **Usage**: Before solving, extract features → predict hyperparameters → inject into solver.
    96	
    97	### 3. Route Quality Predictor (`ml::quality_predictor`)
    98	
    99	**New capability**  
   100	**Research basis**: RouteFinder encoder + gap prediction
   101	
   102	**Design**:
   103	- **Input**: Instance features (same 28-dim vector).
   104	- **Output**: Predicted gap to optimal (%) and expected tour length (km).
   105	- **Model**: Small MLP (28→64→32→2) in Candle.
   106	- **Usage**:
   107	  - Early stopping: if predicted gap < threshold, skip expensive local search.
   108	  - Solver spawning: if predicted quality of default solver is poor, automatically spawn Or-Opt.
   109	
   110	### 4. Graph Embeddings for Road Networks (`ml::graph_embed`)
   111	
   112	**New capability**  
   113	**Research basis**: GAIN (2107.07791) + RRNCO (2503.16159)
   114	
   115	**Design**:
   116	- **Representation**: Line-graph of OSM road network (roads → nodes, junctions → edges).
   117	- **Features per road segment**: length, speed limit, road class one-hot, geometry sinuosity, elevation variance.
   118	- **Model**: 2-layer GraphSAGE-MEAN (Candle) or pre-trained PyTorch → ONNX → Candle.
   119	- **Usage**: Fused into distance/duration matrix for VRP. Edge weights become `haversine * (1 + learned_factor)`.
   120	
   121	### 5. NLP Query Parser (`nlp`)
   122	
   123	**New capability**  
   124	**Research basis**: From Words to Routes (2403.10795)
   125	
   126	**Design**:
   127	- **Approach**: Small fine-tuned LLM (Qwen2.5-1.5B or similar) served via Candle, or rule-based NLU + entity extraction.
   128	- **Input**: "Route 50 packages with 5 vans starting at 45.5,-73.6 by 5pm"
   129	- **Output**: JSON VRP config (`{"num_stops":50,"num_vehicles":5,"depot":[45.5,-73.6],"deadline":"17:00"}`).
   130	- **Training**: Synthetic SFT dataset (template utterances → JSON).
   131	- **Integration**: New `agent` task type `NlpParse`, new MCP tool `parse_routing_query`.
   132	
   133	### 6. Neural-Guided Local Search (`vrp::solvers::neural_guided`)
   134	
   135	**New capability**  
   136	**Research basis**: RLOR (2303.13117) + Analytics & ML in VRP survey (2102.10012)
   137	
   138	**Design**:
   139	- **Wrapper**: Wraps existing 2-Opt / Or-Opt solvers with a neural move selector.
   140	- **Move representation**: For each candidate edge swap, encode the local subgraph (4 nodes + edges) as a feature vector.
   141	- **Model**: Tiny MLP that scores each candidate move. Pick top-k instead of exhaustive/random.
   142	- **Training**: REINFORCE / PPO on synthetic instances where reward = improvement in tour length.
   143	
   144	---
   145	
   146	## Data Flow
   147	
   148	```
   149	User Input
   150	    ├── NLP Query ──→ nlp::parse() ──→ VRP Config JSON
   151	    │
   152	    └── JSON Task ──→ agent::run()
   153	                        │
   154	                        ▼
   155	            Extract ──→ Clean ──→ Compile ──→ Optimize
   156	                │                           │
   157	                ▼                           ▼
   158	        ml::graph_embed()           ml::features::extract()
   159	                │                           │
   160	                ▼                           ▼
   161	        Edge embeddings           selector::predict()
   162	                                        │
   163	                                        ▼
   164	                              quality_predictor::predict()
   165	                                        │
   166	                                        ▼
   167	                              automl::tune_hyperparams()
   168	                                        │
   169	                                        ▼
   170	                              Spawn best solver + best params
   171	                                        │
   172	                                        ▼
   173	                              score_route() → feedback loop
   174	```
   175	
   176	---
   177	
   178	## MCP Server Integration
   179	
   180	### New MCP Tools
   181	
   182	| Tool | Description | Model |
   183	|------|-------------|-------|
   184	| `predict_solver` | **Upgraded** — learned ensemble selector | MLP (Candle) |
   185	| `predict_quality` | Predict expected gap / tour length before solving | MLP (Candle) |
   186	| `tune_hyperparams` | Predict best hyperparameters for this instance | Ridge/MLP |
   187	| `graph_embed_network` | Embed a road network (.rmp or GeoJSON) | GraphSAGE |
   188	| `parse_routing_query` | NL → structured VRP config | Small LLM / NLU |
   189	| `neural_vrp_solve` | Solve VRP with neural constructive heuristic | RouteFinder-style |
   190	
   191	### Existing Tool Upgrades
   192	
   193	| Tool | Change |
   194	|------|--------|
   195	| `predict_solver` | Replace rule-based with learned model; add `use_model` flag |
   196	| `score_route` | Add predicted-vs-actual gap for feedback logging |
   197	| `route_embedding` | Expand from 12-dim to 28-dim research-backed features |
   198	
   199	---
   200	
   201	## Training & Model Lifecycle
   202	
   203	### Offline Training (Python → Rust)
   204	
   205	```
   206	1. Generate / download training data
   207	   - CVRPLIB instances (http://vrp.atd-lab.inf.puc-rio.br/)
   208	   - Synthetic instances (Kool et al. 2019 generator)
   209	   - OSM road networks (osmnx)
   210	
   211	2. Label instances
   212	   - Run all 5 solvers × 20 hyperparam configs per instance
   213	   - Record best solver, best params, achieved gap
   214	
   215	3. Train models (PyTorch / XGBoost)
   216	   - Solver selector: LightGBM or small MLP
   217	   - Quality predictor: Ridge / MLP
   218	   - AutoML: Multi-output Ridge
   219	   - Graph embeddings: PyTorch Geometric GraphSAGE
   220	
   221	4. Export to Rust
   222	   - MLP weights → Candle safetensors
   223	   - XGBoost → JSON dump → Rust parser
   224	   - GraphSAGE → ONNX → Candle
   225	
   226	5. Commit models to repo (or fetch from HF Hub)
   227	```
   228	
   229	### Online Learning (Future)
   230	
   231	- Log every solve: instance features → solver → params → achieved quality.
   232	- Periodic retraining (weekly) on accumulated logs.
   233	- A/B test new model versions against rule-based baseline.
   234	
   235	---
   236	
   237	## Implementation Roadmap
   238	
   239	### Phase 1: Core ML Infrastructure (v0.5.0)
   240	- [ ] `ml::features` — 28-dim instance feature extraction
   241	- [ ] `ml::selector` — Candle MLP solver selector (replaces rule-based)
   242	- [ ] `ml::quality_predictor` — Candle MLP gap predictor
   243	- [ ] `ml::automl` — Ridge regression hyperparameter tuner
   244	- [ ] MCP tool upgrades (`predict_solver`, `route_embedding`)
   245	
   246	### Phase 2: Graph & NLP (v0.6.0)
   247	- [ ] `ml::graph_embed` — GraphSAGE on line-graphs (PyTorch → ONNX → Candle)
   248	- [ ] `nlp` — Synthetic SFT dataset + small LLM inference
   249	- [ ] `parse_routing_query` MCP tool
   250	- [ ] `graph_embed_network` MCP tool
   251	
   252	### Phase 3: Neural Solvers (v0.7.0)
   253	- [x] `vrp::solvers::neural_guided` — Neural move selector for 2-Opt/Or-Opt
   254	- [ ] `neural_vrp_solve` MCP tool
   255	- [ ] Online learning loop from solve logs
   256	
   257	---
   258	
   259	## Dependencies
   260	
   261	### New Rust crates
   262	```toml
   263	# In Cargo.toml [dependencies]
   264	candle-core = { version = "0.10", optional = true }
   265	candle-nn = { version = "0.10", optional = true }
   266	# Consider adding:
   267	# ndarray = "0.15"       # Feature engineering helpers
   268	# linfa = "0.7"          # ML primitives (if we want Ridge in pure Rust)
   269	```
   270	
   271	### External tools (training only)
   272	- Python 3.10+, PyTorch, PyTorch Geometric, XGBoost, Optuna
   273	- `osmnx` for road network extraction
   274	- `cvrplib` for benchmark instances
   275

   277	
   278	## Benchmarking & Validation
   279	
   280	### Metrics
   281	- **Solver selection accuracy**: % of instances where selected solver = best solver
   282	- **Gap improvement**: avg. gap to BKS with learned selector vs. rule-based vs. always-default
   283	- **Inference latency**: <1ms per instance (target)
   284	- **Quality prediction MAE**: mean absolute error of predicted gap (%)
   285	
   286	### Test sets
   287	- CVRPLIB X-n instances (small/medium/large)
   288	- Synthetic uniform & clustered instances (n=20,50,100,200)
   289	- Real-world Montreal road network instances

   292	
   293	## Security & Robustness
   294	
   295	- All ML inference is deterministic (no randomness in production inference).
   296	- Models are versioned; new models require explicit opt-in (`--ml-model-version v2`).
   297	- Fallback to rule-based selector if model file is missing or inference fails.
   298	- Input validation: clamp all features to training distribution bounds to avoid out-of-distribution crashes.

    20	def download_file(url, dest):
    21	    if os.path.exists(dest):
    22	        return
    23	    print(f"Downloading {url} -> {dest}")
    24	    r = requests.get(url)
    25	    r.raise_for_status()
    26	    with open(dest, "wb") as f:
    27	        f.write(r.content)
    28	
    29	def parse_vrp(path):
    30	    with open(path, "r") as f:
    31	        lines = f.readlines()
    32	    
    33	    coords = {}
    34	    demands = {}
    35	    capacity = 0
    36	    section = None
    37	    
    38	    for line in lines:
    39	        line = line.strip()
    40	        if not line: continue
    41	        if line.startswith("CAPACITY"):
    42	            capacity = int(line.split(":")[1])
    43	        elif line.startswith("NODE_COORD_SECTION"):
    44	            section = "coords"
    45	            continue
    46	        elif line.startswith("DEMAND_SECTION"):
    47	            section = "demand"
    48	            continue
    49	        elif line.startswith("DEPOT_SECTION"):
    50	            section = "depot"
    51	            continue
    52	        elif line.startswith("EOF"):
    53	            break
    54	        
    55	        if section == "coords":
    56	            parts = line.split()
    57	            if len(parts) >= 3:
    58	                idx = int(parts[0])
    59	                # CVRPLIB coordinates are usually Euclidean, but we'll treat them as Lat/Lon 
    60	                # scaled to be in a reasonable range (e.g. around Montreal 45, -73)
    61	                coords[idx] = (45.0 + float(parts[2]) / 1000.0, -73.0 + float(parts[1]) / 1000.0)
    62	        elif section == "demand":
    63	            parts = line.split()
    64	            if len(parts) >= 2:
    65	                demands[int(parts[0])] = float(parts[1])
    66	                
    67	    return coords, demands, capacity
    68	
    69	def write_csv(coords, demands, path):
    70	    with open(path, "w") as f:
    71	        f.write("lat,lon,label,demand,type\n")
    72	        for idx in sorted(coords.keys()):
    73	            lat, lon = coords[idx]
    74	            demand = demands[idx]
    75	            role = "depot" if idx == 1 else "stop"
    76	            f.write(f"{lat},{lon},node_{idx},{demand},{role}\n")
    77	
    78	def run_solver(rmp_path, csv_path, solver_id):
    79	    cmd = [
    80	        "./target/release/rmpca",
    81	        "--json",
    82	        "optimize",
    83	        "--mode", "vrp",
    84	        "--input", rmp_path,
    85	        "--coordinates", csv_path,
    86	        "--solver", solver_id,
    87	        "--vehicles", "25" # Hardcoded for this instance for now
    88	    ]
    89	    try:
    90	        result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
    91	        return json.loads(result.stdout)
    92	    except Exception as e:
    93	        print(f"Solver {solver_id} failed: {e}")
    94	        return None
    95	
    96	def main():

    98	    instance_path = "data/cvrplib/X-n101-k25.vrp"
    99	    csv_path = "data/cvrplib/X-n101-k25.csv"

   102	    coords, demands, capacity = parse_vrp(instance_path)
   103	    write_csv(coords, demands, csv_path)
   104	    
   105	    # We need an .rmp file. Let's create a dummy one if it doesn't exist.
   106	    rmp_path = "data/cvrplib/dummy.rmp"
   107	    if not os.path.exists(rmp_path):
   108	        # Create a tiny GeoJSON and compile it
   109	        geojson = {
   110	            "type": "FeatureCollection",
   111	            "features": [{
   112	                "type": "Feature",
   113	                "geometry": {"type": "LineString", "coordinates": [[-73.0, 45.0], [-73.1, 45.1]]},
   114	                "properties": {"highway": "residential"}
   115	            }]
   116	        }
   117	        with open("data/cvrplib/dummy.geojson", "w") as f:
   118	            json.dump(geojson, f)
   119	        subprocess.run(["./target/release/rmpca", "compile", "--input", "data/cvrplib/dummy.geojson", "--output", rmp_path], check=True)
   120	
   121	    solvers = ["clarke_wright", "sweep", "two_opt", "or_opt", "default"]
   122	    results = {}

   131	            }

crossterm = { version = "0.28", optional = true }

dirs = { version = "5.0", optional = true }
shellexpand = { version = "3.1", optional = true }

candle-nn = { version = "0.10", optional = true }
candle-transformers = { version = "0.10", optional = true }

parquet = { version = "54", features = ["async"], optional = true }
arrow = { version = "54", optional = true }
futures-util = "0.3"
geo-types = "0.7"
geo-traits = "0.2"
geo = "0.28"
geojson = "0.24"
wkb = "0.8"
tokio = { version = "1", default-features = false, features = ["sync", "macros", "rt-multi-thread"] }
sqlx = { version = "0.8", features = ["runtime-tokio", "tls-native-tls", "postgres", "chrono", "json"], optional = true }
sha2 = "0.10"
hex = "0.4"
tracing = "0.1"
tracing-subscriber = "0.3"
crc32fast = "1.4"
petgraph = "0.6"
rstar = "0.12"
ordered-float = "4.2"

regex = "1"

{"content":"# /// script

"""
Offline training pipeline for v2rmp Neural Models -- TRAINED ON REAL SOLVER DATA.

Consumes data/training_data.jsonl generated by `cargo run --bin generate-training-data`.
Each line is a JSON object with:
  - features: 28-dim Vec<float>
  - best_solver: string
  - best_distance_km: float
  - solver_dists: [{solver: str, distance: float}, ...]
  - n_stops, n_vehicles, objective

Trains:
  1. Solver Selector: CLASSIFIER with class-weighted CrossEntropyLoss
  2. Quality Predictor: regression on best_distance_km + gap vs default solver
  3. AutoML Predictor: regression on heuristic-informed hyperparams
  4. Move Scorer: regression on synthetic move data
  5. GraphSAGE: placeholder identity weights

Exports Candle-compatible safetensors.
"""

import os
import json
import math
import time
import numpy as np
from safetensors.numpy import save_file

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Load real training data
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

SOLVER_IDS = ["default", "clarke_wright", "sweep", "or_opt", "two_opt", "neural_guided"]
SOLVER_TO_IDX = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(SOLVER_IDS)}

def load_training_data(path="data/training_data.jsonl"):
    """Load JSON-lines training data produced by Rust generator."""
    entries = []
    with open(path, "r") as f:
        for line in f:
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            entries.append(json.loads(line))
    return entries

def prepare_real_labels(entries):
    """Convert raw entries into numpy matrices for training.
    
    CLASSIFICATION formulation: the selector predicts the best_solver directly.
    CrossEntropyLoss with class weights handles label imbalance.
    """
    n = len(entries)
    X = np.zeros((n, 28), dtype=np.float32)
    Y_cost      = np.zeros((n,), dtype=np.int64)       # class label index
    Y_quality   = np.zeros((n, 2), dtype=np.float32)
    Y_automl    = np.zeros((n, 5), dtype=np.float32)

    move_instances = []

    for i, e in enumerate(entries):
        X[i] = np.array(e["features"], dtype=np.float32)

        # Best solver class label
        best = e["best_solver"]
        Y_cost[i] = SOLVER_TO_IDX.get(best, 0)

        # Build solver-distance map
        dists = {sd["solver"]: float(sd["distance"]) for sd in e["solver_dists"]}
        best_dist = min(dists.values())
        worst_dist = max(dists.values())

        # Quality predictor labels
        gap_pct = 0.0
        if worst_dist > best_dist:
            normalized_gap = (worst_dist - best_dist) / (worst_dist + 1e-6)
            gap_pct = normalized_gap * 50.0
        tour_norm = min(best_dist / 5000.0, 1.0)
        Y_quality[i, 0] = gap_pct / 50.0
        Y_quality[i, 1] = tour_norm

        # AutoML labels (heuristic based on instance stats)
        n_stops_norm = X[i, 0]
        density_norm = X[i, 5]
        capacity_ratio = X[i, 19]
        Y_automl[i, 0] = n_stops_norm
        Y_automl[i, 1] = 0.3 + density_norm * 0.4
        Y_automl[i, 2] = 0.1 + capacity_ratio * 0.3
        Y_automl[i, 3] = 0.9
        Y_automl[i, 4] = 0.15

        moves = generate_synthetic_moves_from_features(X[i], n_stops_norm)
        move_instances.extend(moves)

    return X, Y_cost, Y_quality, Y_automl, move_instances

def generate_synthetic_moves_from_features(features, n_stops_norm):
    """Generate synthetic 2-opt move features heuristically from instance stats."""
    moves = []
    n = max(int(n_stops_norm * 500), 10)
    for _ in range(min(n, 50)):
        d_ab = np.random.rand() * 10.0
        d_cd = np.random.rand() * 10.0
        d_ac = np.random.rand() * 10.0
        d_bd = np.random.rand() * 10.0
        delta = (d_ac + d_bd) - (d_ab + d_cd)
        avg_edge = max((d_ab + d_cd + d_ac + d_bd) / 4.0, 1e-6)

        feat = np.zeros(16, dtype=np.float32)
        feat[0] = d_ab
        feat[1] = d_cd
        feat[2] = d_ac
        feat[3] = d_bd
        feat[4] = delta
        feat[5] = d_ab / avg_edge
        feat[6] = d_cd / avg_edge
        feat[7] = d_ac / avg_edge
        feat[8] = d_bd / avg_edge
        feat[9] = np.random.rand() * 20.0
        feat[10] = np.random.rand()
        feat[11] = np.random.rand() * n_stops_norm * 10
        feat[12] = feat[11] / max(n_stops_norm * 10, 1.0)
        feat[13] = np.random.rand()
        feat[14] = np.random.rand()
        feat[15] = 1.0 if delta < -1e-6 else 0.0

        score = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(delta))
        moves.append((feat, score))
    return moves

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. PyTorch Components
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

try:
    import torch
    import torch.nn as nn
    import torch.nn.functional as F
except ImportError:
    print("WARNING: PyTorch not installed. Falling back to numpy-only training (SLOW).")
    torch = None

class TorchMLP(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim, hidden_dims, output_dim):
        super().__init__()
        layers = []
        prev = input_dim
        for h in hidden_dims:
            layers.append(nn.Linear(prev, h))
            layers.append(nn.ReLU())
            prev = h
        layers.append(nn.Linear(prev, output_dim))
        self.net = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        
        # Init weights like He (Kaiming)
        for m in self.modules():
            if isinstance(m, nn.Linear):
                nn.init.kaiming_normal_(m.weight, nonlinearity='relu')
                nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.net(x)

def to_tensor(arr, dtype=torch.float32):
    return torch.from_numpy(arr).to(dtype)

def train_torch_classifier(name, input_dim, hidden_dims, num_classes, X, Y,
                           epochs=400, lr=0.001, batch_size=64, patience=40):
    print(f"Training {name} (PyTorch classifier)...")
    model = TorchMLP(input_dim, hidden_dims, num_classes)
    
    # Compute class weights for imbalance
    class_counts = np.bincount(Y, minlength=num_classes) + 1e-8
    class_weights = (1.0 / class_counts)
    class_weights = class_weights / class_weights.sum() * num_classes
    print(f"  Class weights: {class_weights.round(3)}")
    
    criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(weight=torch.tensor(class_weights, dtype=torch.float32))
    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=lr, weight_decay=1e-5)
    scheduler = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.ReduceLROnPlateau(optimizer, mode='min', factor=0.5, patience=patience//3)

    n = X.shape[0]
    split = int(0.8 * n)
    idx = np.random.permutation(n)
    train_idx, val_idx = idx[:split], idx[split:]
    X_train, Y_train = X[train_idx], Y[train_idx]
    X_val, Y_val = X[val_idx], Y[val_idx]

    X_train_t = to_tensor(X_train)
    Y_train_t = to_tensor(Y_train, torch.long)
    X_val_t = to_tensor(X_val)
    Y_val_t = to_tensor(Y_val, torch.long)

    best_val_acc = -1.0
    best_state = None
    no_improve = 0

    n_batches = max(X_train.shape[0] // batch_size, 1)

    for epoch in range(epochs):
        model.train()
        epoch_loss = 0.0
        perm = np.random.permutation(X_train.shape[0])
        for b in range(n_batches):
            sl = slice(b * batch_size, (b + 1) * batch_size)
            xb = X_train_t[perm][sl]
            yb = Y_train_t[perm][sl]
            if xb.shape[0] == 0:
                continue
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            logits = model(xb)
            loss = criterion(logits, yb)
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            epoch_loss += loss.item()

        # Validation
        model.eval()
        with torch.no_grad():
            val_logits = model(X_val_t)
            val_loss = criterion(val_logits, Y_val_t).item()
            val_pred = val_logits.argmax(dim=1)
            val_acc = (val_pred == Y_val_t).float().mean().item()

        scheduler.step(val_loss)

        if val_acc > best_val_acc:
            best_val_acc = val_acc
            best_state = {k: v.cpu().numpy().astype(np.float32) for k, v in model.state_dict().items()}
            no_improve = 0
        else:
            no_improve += 1

        if epoch % 40 == 0 or no_improve == 0:
            print(f"  Epoch {epoch:3d} — loss={epoch_loss / n_batches:.4f} val_loss={val_loss:.4f} val_acc={val_acc:.3f}")
        if no_improve > patience:
            print(f"  Early stopping at epoch {epoch}")
            break

    print(f"  Best val accuracy: {best_val_acc:.4f}")
    return best_state

def train_torch_regressor(name, input_dim, hidden_dims, output_dim, X, Y,
                          epochs=300, lr=0.001, batch_size=64, patience=30):
    print(f"Training {name} (PyTorch regression)...")
    model = TorchMLP(input_dim, hidden_dims, output_dim)
    criterion = nn.MSELoss()
    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=lr, weight_decay=1e-4)
    scheduler = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.ReduceLROnPlateau(optimizer, mode='min', factor=0.5, patience=patience//3)

    n = X.shape[0]
    split = int(0.8 * n)
    idx = np.random.permutation(n)
    train_idx, val_idx = idx[:split], idx[split:]
    X_train, Y_train = X[train_idx], Y[train_idx]
    X_val, Y_val = X[val_idx], Y[val_idx]

    X_train_t = to_tensor(X_train)
    Y_train_t = to_tensor(Y_train)
    X_val_t = to_tensor(X_val)
    Y_val_t = to_tensor(Y_val)

    best_val_loss = float('inf')
    best_state = None
    no_improve = 0
    n_batches = max(X_train.shape[0] // batch_size, 1)

    for epoch in range(epochs):
        model.train()
        epoch_loss = 0.0
        perm = np.random.permutation(X_train.shape[0])
        for b in range(n_batches):
            sl = slice(b * batch_size, (b + 1) * batch_size)
            xb = X_train_t[perm][sl]
            yb = Y_train_t[perm][sl]
            if xb.shape[0] == 0:
                continue
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            pred = model(xb)
            loss = criterion(pred, yb)
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            epoch_loss += loss.item()

        model.eval()
        with torch.no_grad():
            val_pred = model(X_val_t)
            val_loss = criterion(val_pred, Y_val_t).item()

        scheduler.step(val_loss)

        if val_loss < best_val_loss:
            best_val_loss = val_loss
            best_state = {k: v.cpu().numpy().astype(np.float32) for k, v in model.state_dict().items()}
            no_improve = 0
        else:
            no_improve += 1

        if epoch % 40 == 0 or no_improve == 0:
            print(f"  Epoch {epoch:3d} — loss={epoch_loss / n_batches:.6f} val_mse={val_loss:.6f}")
        if no_improve > patience:
            print(f"  Early stopping at epoch {epoch}")
            break

    print(f"  Best val MSE: {best_val_loss:.6f}")
    return best_state

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Converters: PyTorch state_dict -> Candle safetensors
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def torch_to_candle_weights(state_dict, prefix="lin"):
    """Convert PyTorch Linear layer weights to Candle (out,in) format.
    PyTorch: weight shape (out, in)
    Candle already uses (out, in) for linear layer via matmul(x, weight^T).
    Mapping names: net.0.weight -> lin1.weight etc.
    """
    mapping = {}
    layer_num = 1
    for key in sorted(state_dict.keys()):
        if 'weight' in key:
            mapping[f"{prefix}{layer_num}.weight"] = state_dict[key]
            layer_num += 1
        elif 'bias' in key:
            # Bias belongs to the previous layer
            layer_num_bias = (int(key.split('.')[1]) // 2) + 1
            mapping[f"{prefix}{layer_num_bias}.bias"] = state_dict[key]
    return mapping

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if __name__ == "__main__":
    if torch is None:
        raise RuntimeError("PyTorch is required for this training pipeline.")

    start = time.time()
    os.makedirs("models", exist_ok=True)
    np.random.seed(42)
    torch.manual_seed(42)

    print("Loading real solver training data...")
    entries = load_training_data("data/training_data.jsonl")
    print(f"  Loaded {len(entries)} instances")

    X, Y_cost, Y_qual, Y_auto, move_instances = prepare_real_labels(entries)
    print(f"  Feature matrix: {X.shape}")

    # --- 1. Solver Selector (Classifier with class-weighted CE) ---
    selector_state = train_torch_classifier(
        "Solver Selector", 28, [128, 64], 6, X, Y_cost,
        epochs=600, lr=0.001, batch_size=64, patience=60
    )
    selector_weights = torch_to_candle_weights(selector_state, prefix="lin")
    save_file(selector_weights, "models/solver_selector.safetensors")

    # Sanity-check on full dataset
    model = TorchMLP(28, [128, 64], 6)
    model.load_state_dict(selector_state)
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        logits = model(torch.from_numpy(X).float())
        pred_idx = logits.argmax(dim=1).numpy()
    true_idx = Y_cost
    print(f"  Argmax accuracy (train): {np.mean(pred_idx == true_idx):.4f}")
    for j, sid in enumerate(SOLVER_IDS):
        n_pred = int(np.sum(pred_idx == j))
        n_true = int(np.sum(true_idx == j))
        print(f"    {sid:15s} pred={n_pred:4d} true={n_true:4d}")

    # --- 2. Quality Predictor ---
    quality_state = train_torch_regressor(
        "Quality Predictor", 28, [64, 32], 2, X, Y_qual,
        epochs=400, lr=0.001, batch_size=64, patience=40
    )
    quality_weights = torch_to_candle_weights(quality_state, prefix="lin")
    save_file(quality_weights, "models/quality_predictor.safetensors")

    # --- 3. AutoML Predictor ---
    automl_state = train_torch_regressor(
        "AutoML Predictor", 28, [64], 5, X, Y_auto,
        epochs=300, lr=0.001, batch_size=64, patience=30
    )
    automl_weights = torch_to_candle_weights(automl_state, prefix="lin")
    save_file(automl_weights, "models/automl.safetensors")

    # --- 4. Move Scorer ---
    move_X = np.array([m[0] for m in move_instances], dtype=np.float32)
    move_Y = np.array([[m[1]] for m in move_instances], dtype=np.float32)
    move_state = train_torch_regressor(
        "Move Scorer", 16, [32, 16], 1, move_X, move_Y,
        epochs=500, lr=0.001, batch_size=256, patience=50
    )
    move_weights = torch_to_candle_weights(move_state, prefix="lin")
    save_file(move_weights, "models/move_scorer.safetensors")

    # --- 5. GraphSAGE Placeholder ---
    sage_weights = {
        'conv1.lin_l.weight': np.eye(64, 10).astype(np.float32) * 0.1,
        'conv1.lin_l.bias': np.zeros(64, dtype=np.float32),
        'conv1.lin_r.weight': np.eye(64, 10).astype(np.float32) * 0.1,
        'conv2.lin_l.weight': np.eye(64, 64).astype(np.float32) * 0.1,
        'conv2.lin_l.bias': np.zeros(64, dtype=np.float32),
        'conv2.lin_r.weight': np.eye(64, 64).astype(np.float32) * 0.1,
    }
    save_file(sage_weights, "models/graph_embed.safetensors")

    elapsed = time.time() - start
    print(f"\nTraining complete. Time: {elapsed:.1f}s")
    print(f"  Models exported to models/")
    print(f"  Solver selector: classifier, {len(entries)} instances")
